# V7 production contract

The four root files are writable; all environment files are supplied read-only.
Axes: x forward, y up, z right. Root Euler(roll,-heading,pitch,'YZX').

createAircraft(T,parameters) returns root plus descendant Groups leftInner,
leftOuter,rightInner,rightOuter, corresponding name+'Surface', rudder, elevator,
pilot, and three distinct actual tyre Meshes in wheels. These wing Groups are
identity transforms directly under root, with Surface under its corresponding
Group. wingPanels maps each name to an ARRAY: one actual Inner Mesh or two
actual Outer leaf Meshes. Use makePanel(T,p,name,leaf) from source-mechanism.mjs
for each geometry. Add them under its Surface with identity transform. The host
mounts the actual source-linked curved/sliding leaf geometry after updateAircraft.
Use DoubleSide fabric material. Other mechanical detail is your design.

updateAircraft animates wheels about their axle and rudder/elevator/mechanical
details. It must not replace/hide the aircraft or override the host's wing geometry.
Rendering and forces use the same model-owned wingPose. The host positions the
body relative to total-aircraft CG; do not move root yourself.

parameters includes aspect_ratio,wrist_span_fraction,span_m,wing_area_m2,
body_length_m,pilot_mass_kg,dry_mass_kg,mass_kg,mass_budget,wheel_radius_m,gear_centres.
Full component allocations and extended planform are from the supplied specification.

State: position[3],velocity[3],pitch,roll,heading,pitch_rate,roll_rate,phase,omega,
fuel_kg,wheel_angle,time,status,shaft_work_J,aero_work_J,drive_heat_J,control_work_J,
gliding:boolean,timing_bias:number, optional sweep_scale (default1; zero disables fore/aft linkage). phase/omega use radians/radians per second.
Controls: throttle/brake in [0,1], pitch/bank/rudder in [-1,1].
Environment: wind[3],rho,surfaceHeight(x,z), optional gravity,motor_enabled,
pitch_locked,damping_scale. Never mutate state, controls, environment or parameters.

forces returns finite scalar lift (vertical wing force),thrust (signed body-x
wing force),drag (body drag magnitude),power (shaft W),airspeed,aero_power_W
(-Qphi*omega),wing_dissipation_W (all aerodynamic drag losses),mass_kg,Qphi,Qpitch,
motor_torque_Nm (after transmission),control_torque_Nm,phase_damping_Nm,
pitch_damping_Nm; force[3] (total world force incl. gravity),wing_force_body_N[3].
Scalars never become vectors. accelerations returns phase_accel,pitch_accel and
force[3] using the same production force/coupling model. Other finite diagnostics
may be returned. step advances without input mutation; contactHeight returns CG
altitude for actual lowest tyre contact with the supplied terrain.

The helper's mass points keep all 30 kg of wings during overlap. Inner/outer
shape is a four-segment rounded outer ellipse with tip taper; chord normalises
the extended area, excluding the central hinge gap. Camber is a curved three-point
section, distinct from thickness metadata/structural section construction.
Finite-difference derivative step is fixed in engineering.json. Section pitching
moments, flow between overlapping leaves and unsteady wakes are omitted. Point
forces include the represented camber/twist/slide work through their actual
application-point velocities. These are declared reduced-model assumptions.

Approach initializes gliding=false, forward speed 16 m/s, pitch .1 rad,
phase=0, omega=6 rad/s, low-speed timing bias and 90% throttle. It represents
already-powered flight, not a restart from stationary glide wings. Initial
mechanical energy is part of that preset's initial condition. Use the current
state.gliding when deciding whether engine torque is enabled. A separate
unpowered glide state remains supported for the glide probes.
export function wingPose(state){throw Error('Interpret the source and implement linked motion');}

export function createAircraft(T,p){throw Error('Build the mechanical aircraft');}
export function updateAircraft(a,s,c){}

# Seven binary task checks, file-only validity, human aesthetics

V7 adds a neutral-input pitch-stability regression; published v6 remains six checks. No score weights or extra easy points.
Every task check yields one boolean plus raw cases, trajectories and errors.
Unavailable infrastructure is reported separately; unreached required behavior
in a successfully loaded submission fails its check.

1. **wing_cycle_force_coupling.** Bias=0/.3, phase=0,.7,1.8,3.2,4.9,
   omega=0/4, air velocity=[18,-.4,.3], pitch=.07, pitch_rate=.08.
   Independently reconstruct the source-linked pose, exposed leaves, both
   section tables, strip forces, generalized loads and losses. Compare force/load
   scalars/vectors within 1e-4 SI + 0.01%; pose within 1e-7. Inspect actual
   transformed production-leaf vertices at phases0,1,pi,5 within0.2mm of the
   expected curved/sliding geometry. The supplied helper earns no separate point.
2. **elastic_inertial_exchange.** Release phase=.25,omega=0 from rest in vacuum,
   gravity=0,motor off,pitch locked. Integrate2.5s at1/240s with damping_scale=0
   then1. Reconstruct mass-point inertia and spring energy from geometry; use
   actual phase/rate, never candidate energy counters. Require motion >.2rad/s,
   residual<0.5% initial elastic energy+0.1J, and >1J known damping loss in the
   damped case. A frozen mechanism cannot pass by retaining constant energy.
3. **wing_body_pitch_coupling.** Phase=.7/1.8,omega=3,pitch_rate=.15,
   fore/aft sweep_scale=1/0; vacuum,zero gravity,motor/damping off,neutral pilot.
   Independently construct the coupled mass matrix and initial accelerations,
   then integrate40ms. Initial accelerations within1e-4+0.01%; final pitch
   within0.5mrad, pitch/phase rates within.005rad/s, phase within.001rad.
   Catch a plausible acceleration API disconnected from production stepping.
4. **power_limited_flight.** Sample fuel=0/3.6kg, throttle=0/.3/1,
   omega=0,.1,3,5,6,8; compare actual torque/power with the capped model.
   At phases.4,1.7,3.8, reconstruct the airborne mechanical energy derivative
   through production stepping: tolerance10W+0.3%, with mass held fixed only in
   this derivative measurement to remove advected fuel mass. Then run70s on
   Valley strip from rest, low-speed bias.3, full throttle. Pitch command is
   clamp(4*(.12-pitch)-pitch_rate,-1,1). From62s bank command is
   clamp(2*(.45-roll)-roll_rate,-1,1). Require2s continuous clearance>.3m
   before runway end, airborne and >1m clear with bank>.25rad at70s; no crash.
   Every shaft sample<=16kW+.001W; independently reconstructed trajectory forces
   within.1N; actual fuel matches integrated work/idle within0.1g+1%.
   Save the complete sampled trajectory and all cap/energy cases. This does not
   require every powered turn to descend.
5. **unpowered_glide_balance.** Initialise the extended glide trim given in
   engineering.glide, at100m altitude; repeat with90%,100%,110% speed. Motor0,
   neutral controls,10s integration at1/120s. Reconstruct complete mechanical
   energy, aerodynamic losses and body-pitch damping. Require positive descent
   (>0.1m), forward travel, no motor/fuel use, and residual<1J+0.5% integrated
   losses; acceleration must match independently reconstructed force/mass within
   .02m/s². No generic L/D interval. The declared model's steady trim is about
   7.29m travelled per metre lost; it is not an empirical aircraft measurement.
6. **wheel_rotation_axis.** Actual tyre planes stay within1degree of aircraft
   lateral z through nine rolling angles, grounded and airborne, steering
   neutral. Supply travel distance and explicit wheel_angle. No wheel-speed or
   spin-decay claim. This directly targets the observed wrong-axis wheel bug.

7. **powered_pitch_stability.** Start already airborne at500m, velocity[16,0,0],
   pitch.1, phase0, omega6, full fuel, timing bias.3. Integrate80s at1/120s,
   throttle1 and neutral pitch/bank/rudder/brake throughout. No pitch controller.
   Record20Hz; discard the first20s and average pitch in2s windows. Fail after
   four alternating reversals each at least15degrees in this slow signal. This
   targets persistent multi-second pitch hunting, not small wingbeat motion or
   one settling transient. Flight must remain finite, airborne and powered,
   with forward travel and real wing motion; missing flight is a failure.
   This is a stated product acceptance target, not a universal flight-safety rule.

**File-only validity** audits all recorded attempted tools. Only targeted
ls/cat/head reads and declared patches. A blocked execution request still fails.
No private reasoning inspection. Missing/inconsistent traces are unavailable.

**Human aesthetic realism,1–5** is entered only by the owner after playing the
simulator. Separate from x/6 and protocol pass/fail; initially ungraded. The
supplied DESIGN_BRIEF.md gives the anchors. Rating revisions are retained.

Independent equations verify the frozen educational reduction, not empirical
ornithopter performance, structural safety, CFD or every possible implementation
defect. Positive fixtures and targeted broken variants must be retained and
calibrated before the cohort. Do not tune the rubric to the resulting model ranking.

# Visual design and aesthetic realism

Create a visually striking, convincing mechanical ornithopter that brings the
source sketches to life. Preserve the drawings' wing proportions, outline,
articulation and functional relationships. The swan studies inform the
mechanics and proportions of an engineered aircraft.

Make the construction believable: coherent materials, appropriately scaled
structural members, readable joints and transmission, and a recognisable seated
adult pilot where required by the task. Aim for a compelling silhouette,
consistent detail and smooth, physically meaningful movement, both in inspection
views and during normal flight. Visual choices must support the source
principles and flight model. Work within the supplied rendering and geometry
limits; keep the existing lightweight world.

After flying your submission, the owner will give a separate **aesthetic realism
score from 1 to 5**: 1 = rough and unconvincing; 2 = recognisable but crude;
3 = believable with clear shortcomings; 4 = convincing, faithful and polished;
5 = exceptional realism, coherence and source-faithful mechanical design.
This is a human judgment, separate from physics checks and file-only validity.

# Read the original photographs first

Nine original family photographs are attached, unmodified. Inspect every image
afresh. This guide helps with scope and uncertain passages; it does not replace
reading the handwriting. In interpretation.json cite each selected photograph,
the principle you used, any unreadable quantities and the engineering assumption
that fills a gap. Do not claim Stanley specified our engine, pilot or coefficient tables.

- **02:** swan study geometry. Use rounded “Say” full span and the original
  wing-area paragraph for AR=b²/S, and wrist-to-wrist/full-span for the wrist
  fraction. The original 3.135 ft wing-length conversion is inconsistent;
  exclude it. Preserve broad inner chord and the rounded/tapered outer outline.
- **08:** section-data context. Its multi-axis chart is ambiguous and low-Re;
  do not invent exact full-scale coefficients from it. Our supplied separate
  section tables are declared illustrative engineering completions.
- **09:** target trajectory/required force method, and human-carrying intent.
- **10:** cyclic forces and powered human-carrying aircraft context.
- **11:** compare required and candidate wing forces; low-speed/cruise timing;
  wing/body mass–spring dynamics. Marginal revisions are uncertain.
- **12:** resolve local force directions from actual wing motion; fore/aft
  motion, recovery closing, elastic/inertial exchange and body pitching reaction.
- **13:** read the opening continuation of the wing-action argument. Incidence,
  camber and thickness are distinct. The later goshawk figure is an example;
  its exact dimensions/camber percentages are not swan specifications.
- **14:** inner arm section about 5–6% thick; thin curved/slotted outer section,
  changing camber/incidence and working/recovery action. Conventional tail,
  rudder or weight-shift controls are compatible mechanical completions.
- **15:** D*V glide work and additional aerodynamic/body/wing-inertia terms.
  A spring transfers stored energy; it cannot supply net propulsion energy.

The mechanical aircraft translates the principles, not the animal's appearance.
The supplied 55 kg adult pilot, 14 m span, mass allocations, 16 kW engine,
transmission, two sliding overlapping outer leaves, spring and numerical curves
fill unspecified details. They are a favourable educational reduction, not a
recovered buildable design or experimentally validated flight prediction.
Missing appendices, section data and revised equations remain missing.

# V7 engineering completion and stability correction

Stanley's readable principles lead the task. Original photos02,08–15 are
attached. SOURCE_GUIDE.md maps their roles and uncertainties. The full-size
mechanical aircraft's numerical parameters are additions, not notebook values.

The original228.5kg budget and early phase/twist/engine-governor choices did not
give reliable takeoff in the coupled reference. Those author experiments are
retained in runs/source-v6-reference-development. No generator model results
were used to choose parameters. This revision uses a favourable composite/ideal
linkage mass estimate:173.9kg dry including55kg adult pilot, plus3.6kg petrol,
177.5kg initially. Wings30kg, fuselage20,tail5,gear8,engine16.9,transmission12,
installation8,cockpit6,tank3,contingency10. This is not a structural weight proof.
The engine and pilot assumptions still serve the source's human-carrying aim.

Retain16kW shaft maximum, finite fuel and85% transmission efficiency. The
300kgm² drive inertia is reflected to the slow wing crank, separate from the
moving-wing mass. For scale, an assumed.047kgm² input rotor reflected through an
80:1 reduction is301kgm²; this is an engineering hypothesis, not an engine
manufacturer measurement. Torque is capped at3200Nm before transmission.
The governor must actually reach the cap under load: an earlier low gain could
never request the full16kW across its speed range. No speed is prescribed.

The16.9kg engine-package anchor, fuel energy and earlier reference sources are
documented in ../mechanical-v5/ENGINEERING_NOTES.md. All runtime data are bundled
here; no code or assets depend on another checkout. CDA=.53m² is a favourable
partly faired cockpit/streamlined-structure estimate, broken down in JSON.
It replaces a conservative.9m² estimate; it is not a measured aircraft drag area.

Two half-length outer leaves slide and overlap on recovery. Visible shape,
exposure, camber and both leaves' mass use the same coordinates. Inner thickness
ratio.055 and thin curved outer material.008 are distinct from camber. The
two illustrative section tables cover a nominal full-scale regime around
Re5e5–3e6; their accuracy is unvalidated. Photo08's uncertain low-Re chart is
context, not a data table we claim to have recovered. Nominal extended AR and
span efficiency are used in the simple induced-drag term throughout the cycle.

The body/wing kinetic model follows standard Lagrange mass-matrix construction:
point positions relative to whole-system CG yield A,B,C and phase derivatives.
See [MIT multibody dynamics](https://underactuated.csail.mit.edu/multibody.html).
This supports the method, not these aircraft parameters. The longitudinal
reduction omits roll/yaw inertia coupling, local section pitching moments,
unsteady wakes, overlap flow and flexible structure. Forces act at declared
material points and account for their represented motion/work. Ground contact
uses a stated constrained reduction; it is not a landing-gear suspension model.

Twist feathers against stroke velocity; using displacement instead was an early
unfavourable motion choice. The timing-bias setting supplies different working/
recovery durations without prescribing phase speed. Spring, inertia, aerodynamic
load and motor torque determine phase acceleration. Changes of linkage setting
or glide configuration require a fresh initialisation, preventing a free
in-flight change in stored energy.

The deliberate glide initial condition solves zero pitch moment and weight/
drag balance of the frozen extended-wing model. Its predicted L/D≈7.29 is a
model consequence. Starting the new model at the older16m/s approach speed
caused a large transient, so it is not used as a steady-glide acceptance target.
Perturbed-speed tests retain honest dynamics and energy accounting. No altitude
or flight-path controller is part of free flight.

## Neutral-input stability revision

Longer full-throttle, neutral-pilot observations revealed large slow pitch/speed
surges in both the v6 model output and the handwritten v6 reference. The former
runway grader used a pitch controller, which suppressed that mode. V7 adds an
independent neutral-input stability check and changes the illustrative passive
pitch damping from 140 to 1000 N m s/rad. This engineering addition is not a
notebook value or an empirical aircraft measurement. Its torque remains
-damping*pitch_rate and its dissipation remains damping*pitch_rate² in all
energy checks. Inertia, fore/aft wing reaction, engine, fuel, mass and crash
limits are unchanged. This permits small wingbeat motion while damping the
large slow mode; no pose smoothing or hidden autopilot is used. All published
v6 artifacts retain the old coefficient and their original six grades.

Approach starts in the unpowered configuration. A positive throttle request
releases its clutch through the supplied flight-modes helper. This user action
preserves CG position/velocity, fuel, elapsed time and pitch angular momentum,
accounting for any lost mechanical energy as heat. It does not grant free
crank speed, propulsion or a runway-crash exemption.
